person.name: Harold Pemberly-Nash
person.target_direction: Instructional designer / learning experience designer (corporate L&D or K-12 ed-tech curriculum)

roles.employer: Millbrook High School (Millbrook Unified School District)
roles.title: Science Teacher (Chemistry, AP Chemistry, Physical Science); Science Department Chair 2020-2023
roles.context: Comprehensive public high school, ~1,900 students. Teaches 5 sections (~165 students) per year. Department of 11 teachers when he was chair. Also paid summer curriculum writer for the district in 2019 and 2021.

accomplishments.title: Built Canvas chemistry course for remote learning
accomplishments.problem: In March 2020 the district moved fully online with two weeks' notice; chemistry had no digital course and labs could not run in person.
accomplishments.actions: Designed and built a full Chemistry course in Canvas: 42 modules with learning objectives, short screencast mini-lectures (Screencastify), PhET simulation-based virtual labs, auto-graded quizzes, and a consistent weekly module template. Shared the template with the department.
accomplishments.results: All 4 chemistry teachers in the department (including him) adopted the module template for 2020-21; course was reused as the blended backbone after return to in-person.

accomplishments.title: Raised AP Chemistry pass rate
accomplishments.problem: AP Chemistry pass rate (score 3+) had been 58% in 2017 and enrollment was dropping.
accomplishments.actions: Rebuilt the course around backward design: mapped every unit to College Board's Course and Exam Description learning objectives, added weekly spaced-retrieval quizzes and two full timed practice exams, and used item analysis on quizzes to reteach weak topics.
accomplishments.results: Pass rate rose from 58% (2017) to 74% (2023), with enrollment growing from 19 to 31 students over the same period.

accomplishments.title: Self-paced lab safety module
accomplishments.problem: Lab safety orientation was a lecture that took 2 full class periods at the start of each year in every chemistry section, and students forgot rules by October.
accomplishments.actions: Converted it into a self-paced Canvas module with scenario-based branching questions (built with Canvas quiz logic and Google Forms), a short video walk-through, and a mastery quiz requiring 90% to unlock lab access.
accomplishments.results: He estimates orientation now takes about 1 class period instead of 2, across all 5 sections each year; safety contract completion became trackable in the gradebook. No incident data was tracked before or after.

accomplishments.title: District PD workshop on formative assessment with Google Forms
accomplishments.problem: District wanted teachers to use quick formative checks after the 1:1 Chromebook rollout but most staff had not used the tools.
accomplishments.actions: Designed and delivered a 90-minute hands-on professional development session (needs survey beforehand, practice activity, exit ticket), plus a follow-up job aid.
accomplishments.results: Delivered at two district PD days in 2019 to about 60 teachers total; exit-ticket rating averaged 4.6/5.

accomplishments.title: NGSS-aligned physical science unit rewrite (summer curriculum writer)
accomplishments.problem: District's 9th-grade physical science units were not aligned to NGSS performance expectations ahead of state assessment changes.
accomplishments.actions: As a paid summer curriculum writer (2019, 2021), co-wrote 3 of the 8 units with storyline phenomena, assessment rubrics, and teacher guides.
accomplishments.results: Units are used by all 9th-grade physical science teachers in the district's 3 high schools.

accomplishments.title: Department chair: new teacher onboarding
accomplishments.problem: Department had 4 new teachers in two years with no onboarding beyond HR paperwork.
accomplishments.actions: Created a shared onboarding binder (curriculum maps, lab prep procedures, chemical inventory process) and paired each new teacher with a buddy.
accomplishments.results: Qualitative: new teachers described it as the most useful thing they got their first year; adopted by the math department in 2023.

roles.employer: Riverside Middle School (Delta Oaks School District)
roles.title: 7th Grade Science Teacher
roles.context: Title I middle school; ~150 students per year, high proportion of English learners.

accomplishments.title: Sentence frames and visual vocabulary for English learners
accomplishments.problem: English learners struggled with science vocabulary in written lab conclusions.
accomplishments.actions: Developed sentence frames, illustrated word walls, and a CER (claim-evidence-reasoning) graphic organizer used in every lab.
accomplishments.results: Qualitative: shared with the 7th grade team and used by the ELD coordinator as a model; no formal data.

accomplishments.title: Middle school science fair coordination
accomplishments.problem: School had no science fair for several years.
accomplishments.actions: Organized a school science fair with judging rubric and parent volunteers.
accomplishments.results: About 90 students participated in the first year (2013).
